Stardust Strategic Assets, LLC • Class A CDL Family Fleet

The Rolling Sanctuary Fleet

After the December 1990 I-81 black-ice tour bus crash left Ryan O'Connell paralyzed at T10, the family vowed that no outside contractor would ever control their safety or accessibility again. Tyler Wright, Evan Wright, and Holly O'Connell all earned their Class A Commercial Driver's Licenses (with Passenger and Airbrake endorsements) to personally pilot the band's custom barrier-free fleet.

Interstate Touring Flagship • Forged in Sainte-Claire, Québec

1. 2002 Sainte-Claire 45H3 — “The Iron Horse”

60-Inch Mid-Ship Hydraulic Wheelchair Platform Lift

Inspired by the high-deck tri-axle motorcoaches built in Sainte-Claire, Québec, The Iron Horse is an unpainted brushed stainless-steel monolith engineered as a rolling zero-gravity sanctuary. Because its main cabin deck sits 60 inches above the pavement over massive underfloor equipment bays, a custom mid-ship vertical accessibility door houses a heavy-duty hydraulic platform lift that raises Ryan's manual wheelchair effortlessly into the main lounge.

Onboard Sanctuary & Studio Telemetry

  • Widened 36-Inch Center Aisle: Zero-threshold turning radius from the front co-pilot chairs through the galley and rear stateroom.
  • Acoustic Isolation Bunks: Whisper-quiet sensory-safe sleeper bunks and an onboard DAW node linked to Cassidy's synth rack.
  • Featured Release: Midnight Drivers (2001) & Mile Marker 98 (2003).
Launch Customer Serial #001 (2004) & 2015 Successor • Blacksburg & Campus Shuttles

2. 2004 & 2015 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 (Progress Street Shuttles)

Front-Door-Only Low-Floor Architecture & Kneeling Ramp

When navigating narrow campus streets in Blacksburg, Virginia around Progress Street and CPI, a 45-foot interstate motorcoach is impractical. In 2004, The Stardust Engine became the launch customer for Serial #001 of the Prairie Coachworks RLFD30—a 30-foot Restyled Low-Floor Diesel shuttle ordered in a custom front-door-only executive layout (eliminating the rear transit exit door to maximize interior lounge seating and wheelchair securement space).

The 2015 Replacement Coach: When the band returned from hiatus for 2015's Reignition and completed the 2015 Delaware corporate restructure into Stardust Strategic Assets, LLC, the family purchased a brand-new 2015 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 in the same bespoke front-door-only executive spec as their active Blacksburg/CPI shuttle (while preserving the historic 2004 Launch Customer Serial #001 coach in climate-controlled storage at Stardust Studios).

Progress Street Album Cover & Amber LED Matrix

  • Front ADA Ramp: Kneeling air suspension + 5-second flip-out aluminum low-floor wheelchair ramp deployed directly from the front boarding door.
  • Amber LED Destination Signs: Overhead front destination sign reading PROGRESS STREET and side boarding sign reading THE STARDUST ENGINE.
  • Featured Releases: The 2004 Serial #001 coach is immortalized on the cover of Progress Street (2004); its 2015 successor carries the family home from The Crucible after Live at the Crucible (2016).
CPI Campus Transit • Before the Distance: The Story of John & Erin

3. Blue Ridge Transit (CPI Campus Low-Floor Fleet)

In the companion story and curated soundtrack Before the Distance: The Story of John & Erin (portrayed by Ryan and Cassidy O'Connell), fraternal twins John and Erin navigate the steep limestone hills of Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in motorized power wheelchairs—boarding a Blue Ridge Transit low-floor campus bus via its front-door ADA wheelchair ramp in the pouring autumn rain.

🎧 Stream John & Erin Playlist on music.raggiesoft.com ↗ 📖 Read Before the Distance on Book Reader ↗

The Stardust Engine (ERR-001)

Named after the very first song Ryan, Cassidy, Evan, and Tyler wrote together at CPI in 1986—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos (“Stardust”) and the rockets to get you there (“Engine”).
